summary: Focus video titles on direct questions or shocking physical realities rather than abstract scientific phenomena to capture initial interest. Open the first sentence by directly challenging a common assumption or stating a counter-intuitive fact without a preamble. Keep the first sentence under 12 words to maintain high retention during the initial swipe-test window. Avoid passive background setups, multi-clause introductions, or dense introductory definitions in the first three seconds. Target high-curiosity physical anomalies like biology, vehicle safety, or prehistoric mechanics which consistently outperform broad astronomy topics.
winning_hooks: The real T. rex probably couldn't run. Not even a jog.
A car that folds up in a crash keeps you safer than one that doesn't.
Your eyes are leaking right now, and your brain is hiding it.
You are not sad when you chop an onion.
avoid: Pluto seemed like our solar system's edge, yet astronomers are investigating evidence that...
Fossilized bones can last millions of years, but sometimes they hide more than just minerals.
Long, multi-clause contextual background sentences at the start of the script
Abstract space or astronomy topics that lack a direct physical interaction with the viewer
next_experiment: A/B test a T. rex physics video with a 3-word title and immediate negative hook ('T. rex couldn't run') against a standard descriptive title to see if the stayed_pct breaks past the 60% threshold.
